newsitem.title: USA: Four defendants settle SEC insider trading charges.
newsitem.headline: Four defendants settle SEC insider trading charges.

text.p: Four people accused of insider trading in Century MediCorp Inc stock have agreed to settle charges with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the SEC said on Thursday.

Four of six defendants -- former Century chief executive officer Jacob Terner, his alleged "tippee" Nissan Kahen, Kahen's alleged tippee, Parviz Kahen, and Andrea Dutton -- have, without admitting or denying the allegations, agreed to pay a total of $789,255 in fines and are enjoined from any further antifraud violations, it said in a statement.

On Wednesday, the SEC filed a complaint in U.S. district court in Los Angeles alleging insider trading in Century MediCorp stock just prior to the company's acquisition in July 1992 by Foundation Health Corp.
The SEC said it is also seeking permanent injunctions, disgorgement and penalties from two remaining defendants, former Century board member Theodore Dutton and his alleged tippee, George D. Voigt.
